messages:
erin: Hey — I have a ~2GB nsys + perfetto bundle for a kernel-selection + KV-cache hotloop regression. It contains some customer IDs. Where should I upload and how should I annotate/redact it?

gabe: s3 is fine but use the evidence bucket. Path convention we use: s3://redwood-evidence/eng-runtime/perf/<case-id>/traces/<filename>.tgz. Make sure ACL is private and only eng-runtime + sec can access.

erin: case id is PERF-4821. Filename currently: 2026-03-18_erin_nsys_perfetto.tgz. Any naming tweaks?

kevin: include a short descriptor and kernel hint. Example: PERF-4821_erin_nsys-kernel-timeline_kvcache-thrash_20260318.tgz. Put a metadata JSON next to the blob with fields: team, case_id, root_ts, model, hw, kernel_hint. (We attach as s3 metadata x-amz-meta-... or as a small .meta.json file in same folder).

perf-bot: Reminder: do NOT upload unredacted customer PII to public buckets. Use redact tools in docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/tools/trace-redact. Also for large uploads use multipart copy, see #eng-infra upload guide. :warning:

mikhail: For the customer IDs in perfetto trace you can use the redact script to replace long hex/uuid patterns and URLs. Example commands:```bash
# unzip bundle, run scrub then re-tar
tar xzf 2026-03-18_erin_nsys_perfetto.tgz
./tools/trace-redact/scrub_perfetto.sh traces/*.pftrace
# simple sed mask for JSON blobs inside trace metadata
find traces -type f -name '*.json' -exec gsed -E -i 's/([A-Fa-f0-9]{8,})/REDACTED_HEX/g' {} +
tar czf PERF-4821_erin_nsys-kernel-timeline_kvcache-thrash_20260318.tgz traces/ metadata.json
```

erin: Nice. Any guidance on what to annotate in the timeline for kernel selection? I want reviewers to quickly see where the wrong kernel was picked + kvcache churn.

gabe: Add a short README.md or metadata JSON with: kernel_selection_hint: "unexpected_sm75_matmul_fallback", timeline_ranges: ["0:00:12-0:00:24","0:01:10-0:01:18"], kvcache_events: "high-evict-rate at 0:00:30", command line used, model name, seq len distribution. Keep these keys small.

kevin: If you can, attach a small perf summary image (png) highlighting hotspots and annotate the pixel times (helps quick triage). Put it next to the bundle as PERF-4821_summary.png.

ops-bot: For uploads >1GB use presigned multipart: https://infra-docs/upload-multipart. If you need a temporary presigned URL reply here with size and I'll create one (expires 24h).

erin: Can someone run an initial scrub and confirm there's no tenant ids left? I can run scrub script but want a second eye.

mikhail: I'll spot-check after you run scrub. Ping me once you upload to s3 path and leave the object in a "quarantine" prefix so only reviewers can access: s3://redwood-evidence/eng-runtime/perf/quarantine/PERF-4821/...

gabe: Also include the nsys metadata (.qdrep) and a short cmdline block in the README. Example:```text
nsys profile --output=trace --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt -f true --sample=none --compress true <your-run>
```

erin: uploading now after scrub. I'll post the s3 path + metadata.json and ping @mikhail. Thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Upload checklist: 1) scrub/redact done 2) metadata.json present 3) private ACL 4) reviewers listed in object ACL 5) attach summary image 6) tag with "perf_evidence".

mikhail: Got it — will review once you drop the presigned link.

ops-bot: Note: retention for evidence buckets is 365 days by default; set lifecycle if you need shorter retention.

erin: Done. Path: s3://redwood-evidence/eng-runtime/perf/quarantine/PERF-4821/PERF-4821_erin_nsys-kernel-timeline_kvcache-thrash_20260318.tgz. Metadata posted at s3://redwood-evidence/eng-runtime/perf/quarantine/PERF-4821/metadata.json. Pinged @mikhail.

mikhail: Verified scrub: no obvious UUIDs, IPs, or tenant tokens in the JSON. Proceeding with quick triage now.

gabe: When you write the postmortem link later, add a pointer to this evidence path and include the key metadata fields so infra can find it programmatically.

erin: will do. Thanks everyone.
